newsitem.title: POLAND: NBP SELLS PLN 91 MLN OF BONDS AT OUTRIGHT.
newsitem.headline: NBP SELLS PLN 91 MLN OF BONDS AT OUTRIGHT.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland sold 70 million zlotys of 17-percent two-year fixed bonds, due July 12, 1997, after Polish banks bid for 96 million of the bonds, the central bank said.
The bank also sold 21 million zlotys of its 14-percent five-year bonds after banks placed 47 million worth of bids.
The central bank offered 231 million zlotys of the shorter bonds and 199 million zlotys of the longer paper.
The minimum price of the two-year paper was 99.39, up from 99.34 on August 23 and the average price was 99.43, up from 99.38.
The minimum price of the five-year bond was 90.15, up from 90.04 on August 22 and the average price was 90.19, up from 90.04.
The settlement date is August 27, 1996 by 0900 local time.
